Their capacity genuinely rises from the recorded first discharge, so the drift is in the data, not only in the reference; B0054 also stays above the ceiling. The four G7 cells return under the beginning-of-life peak alone, because their reading above the {{rsc_ceiling:.0f}}% ceiling was a high first cycle sitting above the early median rather than a real rise. ## What it predicts

Three things from measurements a battery management system can actually take. A **partial-window SOH** (percent) from the {{mc_window_high:.1f}}–{{mc_window_low:.1f}} V window alone — the majority of a discharge's capacity on the warm cells and about a quarter on the cold one, not a small early slice — read before the discharge finishes. An **indicative remaining life** in sequential discharges, reported as a range, not a point. And the **window formula** it is scored against, the best a BMS can compute from the window alone.

## How partial the window is

Calling this a "partial discharge" is not a claim that the window is small. Averaged over the {{mc_wp_n_cells:d}} kept cells the {{mc_wp_window_high:.1f}}–{{mc_wp_window_low:.1f}} V window holds {{mc_wp_capacity_mean:.1f}}% of each discharge's capacity and {{mc_wp_time_mean:.1f}}% of its time. It is not uniform: the warm G1 cells hold most of their capacity in the window, while the cold G9 cell traverses the band early and holds little.

## Conditions tested

- Constant-current discharges at the three kept operating conditions: G1 {{mc_g1_temp:d}} °C / {{mc_g1_amp:d}} A, G3 {{mc_g3_temp:d}} °C / {{mc_g3_amp:d}} A, G9 {{mc_g9_temp:d}} °C / {{mc_g9_amp:d}} A.
- The {{mc_random_n:d}} random-load cells the audit keeps (B0039, B0042–B0044), scored with the shipped model but never trained on.
- Sensor noise added to a held-out cell's inputs: Gaussian voltage noise up to {{mc_largest_mv:.0f}} mV and Gaussian current noise up to {{mc_largest_pct:.0f}}% of each sample's current.
- The trained window and two narrower windows: {{mc_window_high:.1f}}–{{mc_window_low:.1f}} V (trained), {{mc_narrow_0_hi:.1f}}–{{mc_narrow_0_lo:.1f}} V and {{mc_narrow_1_hi:.1f}}–{{mc_narrow_1_lo:.1f}} V (tested at inference).
- A model trained on each candidate window ({{mc_wtband_0_hi:.1f}}–{{mc_wtband_0_lo:.1f}}, {{mc_wtband_1_hi:.1f}}–{{mc_wtband_1_lo:.1f}}, {{mc_wtband_2_hi:.1f}}–{{mc_wtband_2_lo:.1f}}, {{mc_wtband_3_hi:.1f}}–{{mc_wtband_3_lo:.1f}}, {{mc_wtband_4_hi:.1f}}–{{mc_wtband_4_lo:.1f}} V): the smallest that holds the pooled held-out MAE under {{wts_limit:.0f}}% is {{wts_3_8_3_6_hi:.1f}}–{{wts_3_8_3_6_lo:.1f}} V (span {{wts_3_8_3_6_span:.2f}} V) at {{wts_small_all:.2f}}%.

## Conditions NOT tested

- Real packs: no field data, no customer cell, no manufacturer reference and no hardware sign-off.
- Temperatures and currents outside the three tested conditions and the trained current band, which is {{mc_current_low:.1f}}–{{mc_current_high:.1f}} A.
- Duty cycles with rapid, continuous load changes beyond the random-load cells above; only one current level per condition is trained on.
- Multi-cell pack interactions (imbalance, thermal coupling); the live pack monitor is exercised on injected synthetic faults.
- The ESP32 firmware on real hardware, and an external email or pager endpoint — the alert delivery target is a local mock receiver.

## Refusal rules

The estimator returns no number, rather than a guess, when:

- a window is measured outside the trained {{mc_window_high:.1f}}–{{mc_window_low:.1f}} V band (`features.WindowRangeError`);
- fewer than {{mc_min_discharges:d}} opening discharges are available for the cell-relative baseline (`InsufficientReferenceError`);
- the discharge current sits far outside the trained {{mc_current_low:.1f}}–{{mc_current_high:.1f}} A band, where the model has no training data.

#### Cross-condition transfer (leave-one-group-out, partial window only)

**On the partial-discharge task the model does not transfer across conditions when it is trained on raw window features.** A BMS that only watches the partial-discharge window never sees the full discharge, so this is the honest version of the SOH question: predict SOH from the window alone.
With the full feature set, leave-one-cell-out within G1 the same ElasticNet model reaches {{cc_in_cell_en_mae:.2f}}% MAE; held out across conditions on raw window features it climbs to as much as {{cc_worst_raw_en_mae:.2f}}%. The table below is that failure, measured, not a model claim.

| Held-out group | Cells | Cycles | ElasticNet MAE (%) | XGBoost MAE (%) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| G1 | {{logo_g1_cells:d}} | {{logo_g1_cycles:d}} | {{logo_g1_en_mae:.2f}} | {{logo_g1_xgb_mae:.2f}} |
| G3 | {{logo_g3_cells:d}} | {{logo_g3_cycles:d}} | {{logo_g3_en_mae:.2f}} | {{logo_g3_xgb_mae:.2f}} |
| B0053 (G9) | {{logo_g9_cells:d}} | {{logo_g9_cycles:d}} | {{logo_g9_en_mae:.2f}} | {{logo_g9_xgb_mae:.2f}} |

**Cell-relative window features recover the transfer, and the model then beats the window formula on the held-out condition.** Because the groups differ in ambient temperature (G1 {{cc_g1_temp:d}} °C, G3 {{cc_g3_temp:d}} °C, G9 {{cc_g9_temp:d}} °C) and current (G1 {{cc_g1_amp:d}} A, G3 {{cc_g3_amp:d}} A, G9 {{cc_g9_amp:d}} A), the raw levels do not line up. Dividing each window quantity by the cell's own first-five-discharge median and by its current puts every cell on the same scale and makes the ElasticNet transfer to a condition it has never seen. #### B0053: one cell, and an R² that says the shape is not learnt

![Predicted versus true SOH for B0053 over discharge index](soh_partial_B0053.png)

B0053 is reported as the single cell it is, plotted predicted against true SOH over discharge index rather than only averaged into a metric. The partial-window XGBoost is close in level — MAE {{pt_b0053_b0053_xgb:.2f}}% — but its R² is {{pt_b0053_b0053_xgb_r2:.2f}}, below even a constant mean, so it does not follow the fade: the low error comes from B0053's narrow SOH range, not from tracking its trajectory. That is the honest reading of the transfer — the cell-relative features carry the operating condition's level to a cell the model has never seen, not its degradation path.

So the claim that only the four G1 cells reach 80% is false in general: four more cells do. They are still not added to the constant-current SOH/RUL training set, because their load and temperature change across the record, so their features are not comparable at a single operating condition; but they are not left out because the model fails on them — the shipped partial-window SOH model transfers to all of them and beats the window formula (see the random-load transfer table under *Key Results*), so the exclusion is a comparability choice. B0041 reaches 80% too but is excluded, and its reference shows why: its opening {{rl_b41_n:d}} recorded discharges carry a median {{rl_b41_early_cap:.3f}} Ah at a mean {{rl_b41_early_cur:.2f}} A — about a quarter of the group's own load — with the terminal voltage falling by only {{rl_b41_drop:.3f}} V, against {{rl_b41_later:.2f}} Ah once the cell discharges normally later in life. Those opening runs are a measurement failure, not a low-capacity cell, but they are the majority of the record, so the rule that keeps only discharges above half the cell's median normalises against them and keeps them; the resulting {{rl_b41_ref:.3f}} Ah reference is an artifact, its SOH rises above the ceiling and the cell is excluded — which is why no cell the pipeline trusts has a reference under half the median of its later valid discharges.

#### One decision: RUL ships as a range, not a point estimate

Neither method wins everywhere. Leave-one-cell-out inside G6, the fleet-lifetime average is the best estimate on all {{ruld_g6_n:d}} cells — MAE {{ruld_g6_base_lo:.1f}}–{{ruld_g6_base_hi:.1f}} discharges — against the matcher's {{ruld_g6_traj_lo:.1f}}–{{ruld_g6_traj_hi:.1f}} and the early-fade extrapolation's {{ruld_g6_extrap_lo:.1f}}–{{ruld_g6_extrap_hi:.1f}}. Trained on G6 and tested across groups on each G1 cell, the matcher beats the fleet-lifetime average on {{ruld_g1_traj_beat:d}} of {{ruld_g1_n:d}} cells; B0006 is the exception, because it fades faster than any reference trajectory. Since the winner depends on the cell and the reference group, no single method is shipped: every discharge carries an indicative range, the minimum to the maximum of the matcher, the early-fade extrapolation and the fleet-lifetime average at that discharge (mean width {{ruld_range_width:.1f}} discharges on the held-out G1 cells).

As an average the longer window looks better — mean MAE falls from {{cgw_mean_w20:.1f}} to {{cgw_mean_w40:.1f}} discharges — but that average is one cell. B0039 barely fades over its first discharges and then knees late, so its line at the default window lands {{cgw_b0039_over:.0f}} discharges past its real end of life; by {{cgw_w40:d}} discharges the fit finally sees the knee and its error drops to {{cgw_b0039_w40:.1f}}. The longer window is therefore not kept; the default stays at {{cgw_w20:d}} discharges.

The figure shows what fails.
